items.stem: Which cell of the tricellular model lies between about 30° and 60° latitude?

items.stem: Explain why biomes shift in latitude with the seasons in some regions.
items.answer: The ITCZ and pressure belts follow the overhead Sun north and south, bringing seasonal rains (e.g. wet and dry seasons in the savanna and monsoon regions).

items.answer: Weather is the short-term state of the atmosphere (hours to days); climate is the average weather over a long period, usually 30 years.

items.answer: The model explains the broad pattern but must be combined with local factors to explain the actual distribution.

items.stem: Compare the Hadley cell with the polar cell.

items.answer: (a) -6.5 °C (b) 1035 + (18 − 10) / 6.5 × 1,000 ≈ 2,266 m (c) temperature falls with altitude as with latitude, so mountains show zones (e.g. forest → montane shrub → alpine grassland/tundra → ice) similar to the sequence from the equator to the poles; precipitation, aspect and soils modify the pattern.
items.markingKey: (a) A1 -6.5. (b) M1 (T − tl)/6.5 × 1,000, A1 ≈ 2,266 m. (c) R1 temperature decrease, R1 analogous zones / named example.

items.stem: In an old-growth oak woodland, community GPP = 2630 g m⁻² yr⁻¹ and total community respiration R = 2630 g m⁻² yr⁻¹. (a) Calculate the P:R ratio and the net productivity of the community. (b) Use your answer to suggest the stage of succession and explain how P:R changes during succession.
items.answer: (a) P:R = 2630/2630 = 1.00; net productivity = 0 g m⁻² yr⁻¹ (b) P:R ≈ 1, little net accumulation, typical of a climax community; P:R starts high in pioneer stages, then falls towards 1 as biomass and respiring tissue accumulate.
items.markingKey: (a) A1 1.00, A1 0. (b) R1 interpretation of ratio, R1 trend during succession.

items.stem: Suggest why the west coast of South America at 20° S is a desert while the Amazon at the same latitude receives over 1,500 mm of rain.
items.answer: Descending Hadley-cell air plus the cold Humboldt Current and the Andes rain shadow keep the Atacama dry; the Amazon receives moist trade winds from the Atlantic.
items.markingKey: Descending Hadley-cell air plus the cold Humboldt Current and the Andes rain shadow keep the Atacama dry; the Amazon receives moist trade winds from the Atlantic.

items.stem: Using the Amazon carbon sink as an example, explain the effect of climate change and land use on biome function.
items.answer: Studies (Gatti et al., 2021) found parts of the south-eastern Amazon have become a net carbon source due to deforestation and drought. Stressed forest loses more carbon through tree death and fire than it gains through growth.
items.markingKey: Context (Studies (Gatti et al., 2021) found parts of the south-eastern Amazon have become a net carbon source due to deforestation and drought.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. items.stem: Describe how you would investigate zonation on a sand-dune system.
items.answer: Lay a tape from the strandline inland; at regular intervals (e.g. every 10 m) place a quadrat and record percentage cover of each species; measure abiotic factors (wind, soil moisture, pH, organic content); repeat transects; present as a kite diagram.

items.stem: With reference to the resource booklet and examples you have studied, evaluate the claim: "Human disturbance always reduces the biodiversity of ecosystems."
items.answer: Severe or frequent disturbance reduces biodiversity, but moderate, traditional management can maintain species-rich plagioclimax communities.
items.markingKey: Strengths / supporting points: deforestation and urbanisation remove habitats; invasive species spread with disturbance. Limitations / counter-points: intermediate disturbance can increase diversity; plagioclimaxes (chalk grassland, hay meadows) are biodiversity-rich. items.stem: Explain how the tricellular model accounts for the distribution of three named biomes. [7]
items.answer: Rainforest (ITCZ rising air), hot desert (descending air at 30°), temperate forest (Ferrel cell, mid-latitude depressions), tundra (polar high, low insolation).

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "A relatively stable community at the end of succession, in equilibrium with the environment"?
items.answer: climax community
items.markingKey: D. This is the definition of climax community.

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "The circulation cell in which warm air rises at the equator (low pressure, high rainfall) and sinks at about 30° latitude (high pressure, deserts)"?
items.answer: Hadley cell
items.markingKey: A. This is the definition of Hadley cell.

items.stem: Which biome contains about half of the world's terrestrial species while covering about 6% of the land surface?
items.answer: Tropical rainforest
items.markingKey: A. High productivity and stable climate support high diversity.

items.stem: Lukas writes: "A transect gives an exact picture of every species in an area." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: A transect samples only a narrow strip; it may miss species and needs repeats to be representative.
items.markingKey: A transect samples only a narrow strip; it may miss species and needs repeats to be representative. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Outline why secondary succession is faster than primary succession.
items.answer: Soil, seed banks, roots and nutrients are already present, so plants can establish quickly without the slow process of soil formation.
items.markingKey: Soil, seed banks, roots and nutrients are already present, so plants can establish quickly without the slow process of soil formation. [1] per valid point, up to [3].

items.stem: Outline why climate change is expected to shift biome boundaries.
items.answer: Changing temperature and precipitation alter the conditions each biome requires; boreal forest is expected to move polewards into tundra, deserts may expand, and species may be unable to migrate fast enough.
items.markingKey: Changing temperature and precipitation alter the conditions each biome requires; boreal forest is expected to move polewards into tundra, deserts may expand, and species may be unable to migrate fast enough. [1] per valid point, up to [3].

items.stem: A student claims: "Rainforest soils are fertile because the vegetation is so lush." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Most nutrients are held in the biomass; once cleared, soils quickly lose fertility through leaching.
items.markingKey: Most nutrients are held in the biomass; once cleared, soils quickly lose fertility through leaching. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: State two differences between zonation and succession.
items.answer: Zonation is the spatial arrangement of communities along an environmental gradient at one time; succession is the temporal change of a community at one place.
items.markingKey: Zonation is the spatial arrangement of communities along an environmental gradient at one time; succession is the temporal change of a community at one place. [1] per valid, explicit comparison up to [3].

items.stem: A student claims: "Succession always ends in forest." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: The climax depends on climate and soils - it may be grassland, tundra or desert scrub where trees cannot grow.
